items.note: Association organized at Larrow Green 1889, Gideon Vose first president, creamery built 1891 (story 1).
Article VII: paid by butterfat by test, not weight; test of the delivering station governs (story 1).
Section A only calls Article VII 'the hinge of everything'. It never says that under payment by weight the fault would have cost nothing. The explicit point appears only in B3.
Only Wilbur Teague is named. Effie Loomis (secretary, minute book) and Hobart Sill (buttermaker) are absent.
Has Selby Vose as Gideon's son, but gives him as manager from 1911, a catalogued planted error. The key requires 1913.
Story 5 (headed 1898-1929): yearly 'station gain ... five and a quarter per cent, as usual, carried to the general account'.
Ostrey Hollow skimming station, seven miles up the valley, opened 4 May 1896, first season on glass borrowed from Larrow Green.
Core of the system present: milk weighed and sampled, tested, cream to Larrow Green, skim returned. Story 8 adds the bottle ruled for the full charge.
Ammon & Sons, Tarnet; invoice 14 April 1897; in use 1 May 1897.
Full invoice itemized: 6 dozen pipettes marked 17.6 c.c. etc., total $77.93.
Story 3: 0.19 short, 'the same in the June flush as in February', 'flat as a floor'.
Never says a pipette cannot be checked without a burette, or that there was no burette in the county.
Ansel Keddie (1861-1934), twenty-nine seasons 1896-1924, dismissed 30 April 1925.
The station test book is kept in Keddie's hand; the gating element is present, though the column detail is thin.
No summary leaf. The 1896 recorded average of 3.80 is never given; 3.80 appears only as the true value. Both figures are required.

Broke 8 May 1911, borrowed measure for nine weeks to 10 July, tests higher then back to the old level, question mark. The 3.80 figure is missing, but the core fact is present (the item has no REQUIRED line).
Married Orra Brant, Emmet's sister; Emmet the largest patron; 'tested his brother-in-law's milk'.
The 1919 circular is present, but Keddie's 17 March 1925 statement ('tested as he was taught, cannot say why') is absent. Both bolded elements are required.
Died February 1934, never cleared; test book impounded 1925 and deposited in the Historical Rooms 1959.
Hessel Bottom, six farms, Emmet Brant's the largest.
Weigh book from 1 January 1897; his scale and the station's agreed.
First complaint on record 1902. Larrow Green 3.78 is given beside 3.61. The 0.19 is always the true shortfall and is never conflated with the Hollow-vs-Green gap.
The committee came in January 1908 and reported in March. The three-month sampling window (January, February and March) is not stated.
1910 leaf: 200,000 lb on a test of 3.42. Story 8 states the error is proportional ('same proportion every time').
Roy Brant lent the weigh book to Ivy in 1958; passed to Hazel on Roy's death in 1962.
Cudd's cheese company at Alder Corners in Vessey County, but 'over the ridge': Redlow Ridge is never named, and the key says the ridge gates.
Four of the six Hessel Bottom farms hauled to Alder Corners in the summer flush. 1915 is not given, but the core fact is present.
'Built-in comparison': Cudd's test book, other county (Vessey), different glass. At least two elements present.
Section A never states the result: the same men's milk tested about 0.19 higher at Alder Corners over sixteen seasons.
Section A never states that the same milk tested differently in two buildings, which kills the hay and water explanations together.
Rosalie Cudd, Jerome's daughter, ran the factory from 1941 and copied its test figures for Ivy in 1958. Core fact present.
Merle Strawn is named on the Ordell circuit, but only 'from 1908' (a planted error). The 1907-1936 span is absent.
Lactometer on every visit, never found water.
12 June 1923, pipettes run against a calibrated burette, whole lot condemned.
Recorded the condemnation and said nothing about the previous twenty-six years; drew no inference.
Gives the 1924 average as 3.85, a planted error. The key requires 3.80.
Crate to the station loft; notebooks in the Farland college library since 1947.
Patrons petitioned January 1925.
Board sat 17 March-4 May 1925, three sittings, two in the station weigh room. The chairman is 'an Ashlin attorney', not named as Frick.
Water, theft by the tester and bog hay all argued; no cause established.
Four books including Strawn's 1923 notebook; nobody laid it beside the receiving book.
Dismissed 30 April 1925; 4 May award of $3,800 'without admission', charged to the station account, no cause established.
One fifth of $19,000 is stated, but not that the award was charged to the very account where the loss had accumulated as 'gain'.
Ivy b. 1931, Duncan's daughter and Ansel's granddaughter, graduate student at Farland under Leland Vaught.
'Pulled the scattered record together': weigh book, Strawn's notebook, Alder Corners figures, crate.
Crate in the loft, February 1958. Nine is left open ('Falke and Oram say nine; the Chronicle says eleven') and never stated.
9 March 1958 against a burette. Story 2 gives 16.72 c.c. vs 17.6, 0.88 short, 5 per cent.
Taken across Section A: 1 May 1897 to 12 June 1923, 5 per cent low, 3.61 where 3.80, 0.19 short, same proportion.
Milk, fat and money are present (40,000,000 lb; 76,000 lb; $19,000 at 25c). The ledger identity (the station-gain entries sum to 76,000 lb) is not stated; all four are required.
Bulletin No. 471, October 1958; cleared 24 years after his death; crate 35 years in the loft.
Granddaughter.
Ivy is Duncan's daughter and Duncan is Ansel's son.
Second cousins, derived via Roy and Duncan as first cousins.
Correctly declines full vs half siblings, but says half siblings would make them 'half second cousins'. The key requires stating that it does not change the answer. No deduction (abstained).
Gideon Vose, his father.
Gideon's Article VII made the station test decisive; the founder's son administered it and accused the patrons.
'No relationship is established ... a negative cannot be proved.' No verdict that they were or were not kin, so treated as an abstention with no -2.
Holds that the family member's denial 'outranks' the talk; the key says a denial is not a record. Does not state that no document names or denies a link.
3.60 true test; 7,200 lb; 360 lb owed.
$90 accepted: explicitly uses the 25c period average because the 1910 price is 'not in the sources', with working shown.
76,000 lb = 5.26% of fat credited and 5.00% of fat received; denominators named.
$77.93 with the addition shown.
72 pipettes, each 0.88 c.c. short.
1 May 1897-12 June 1923 = 26 years 1 month 11 days; 25 full years 1898-1922; part years excluded.
Abstention A02: the first-season intake cannot be determined.
Variable: the station's own measuring glass vs a borrowed one; only the glass changed.
Held constant: herds, pasture/hay, season, tester, method, scales, machinery.
Result given only as 'rose markedly ... fell back'. No 3.80 or 3.61, and the run claims no figures exist for the interval.
Establishes causation in the glass, not cows/hay/water/tester; limits: size of error, which item (pipette or bottle).
Ledger surplus (r23), 1911 interval (r22/r24/r18), 1924 recovery (r22): three valid reasons, three narrators.
Independence claim is flawed on the run's own account: reasons 2, 3 and 4 all rest on the station test book ('the station test book in two separate periods'), and 2 and 3 both on Falke.
Abstention A09 asserted: 'Did the bookkeeper ever question the ledger entries? No.'
Yes, he knew the tests ran low: complaints from 1902, the 1919 circular.

Only two of five hold: signed the station-gain sheets, wrote the 1919 circular. Manager start is given as 1911 (wrong); watering at the hearing is not attributed to him; nothing on his never naming the glass.
Abstention A03 asserted: 'He did not, on the evidence, know what his own ledger said about why', resting on Kyle ruling it out.

Correctly resolved with method: Keddie's start 1895 vs 4 May 1896 (row 1); Orra 1868 vs 1866 by arithmetic (row 7); the 1908 committee 'sat again in 1925' as two bodies (row 16). The circular row is resolved wrongly (eleven).
NT-18 great-niece (r19 + r22), broken by Duncan's genealogy and Falke's retraction; NT-14 $77.39 (r19 + r20), broken by adding the invoice lines. No third pair identified.

A04: why the lot was short cannot be determined, works books burned 1931 (story 2, F1). A10: the adoption year cannot be determined, by-laws undated and minute book lost (story 1). A06, the lender of the 1911 measure, is not addressed.
r18's 1868 vs 'eighty-two in 1948'; r20's 'nothing before 1900' above her 1897 invoice.
1897 pipettes 16.72 vs 17.6, 5 per cent low, proportional (fixed ratio), onset and end with nothing else changing. The cessation figure 3.85 is wrong but is context; it is deducted separately.
Watering (Vose) defeated by Strawn's lactometer and Brant's agreeing scales.
Theft defeated: the ledger shows more fat arriving, not less; 1911 interval; 1924 rise under the same tester.
Bog hay defeated by Bulletin 214 (0.05 in winter, nothing in summer) vs a constant 0.19.
Abstention A07 asserted: 'Did the 1925 board ever examine the condemned glassware? No.'
Abstention A05 asserted: 'Ansel Keddie believed it was "something in the glass."'
Hand count is 153 words (151 even if 'per cent' counts as one word); the run's own 148 is wrong. Over the 150 cap.
Five record series: invoice, weigh book, ledger, (Strawn's) notebooks, 1958 measurement.
No decoy stated as fact and no wrong headline figure in the summary.
5 per cent short, 1897, 76,000 lb/$19,000, 1923, 1958, Ansel and Ivy named.

deductions.reason: Corruption: Selby Vose manager from 1911 (story 4, story 5, B3)
Corruption: Strawn's circuit/lactometer visits from 1908 (story 3, story 6, F2)
Corruption: 1924 station average 3.85 (story 6, C1b, D2, F1)
Corruption: water circular carried to eleven families, F058 (story 5, E row 7)
Gullibility A09: asserts the bookkeeper never questioned the entries (D2)
Gullibility A03: asserts Vose did not know the tests were understated (D3, also story 5 and B3)
Gullibility A07: asserts the board did not examine the glassware (F subsidiary, also story 7)
Gullibility A05: asserts Keddie believed it was the glass (F subsidiary)
